newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Air traffic in Asia set to soar - HK's Tsang.
newsitem.headline: Air traffic in Asia set to soar - HK's Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Tuesday economic growth in the Asia Pacific would fuel global aviation traffic in coming years.

"Economic growth has been the catalyst for expansion of the region's aviation business," Tsang said at an aviation function. "Future prospects look sound with IATA forecasting that by the year 2010, total international scheduled passenger traffic to, from and within Asia Pacific will represent 51.1 percent of the world total," he said.
IATA is the International Air Transport Association.
Tsang also said Hong Kong was working toward concluding a host of air services agreements, which would hold good after the British colony returns to China on July 1, 1997.
Airlines operating from the Kai Tak International Airport offer over 1300 direct round trips each week between Hong Kong and over 100 cities world-wide.
Kai Tak handled over 27 million passengers in 1995.
